owner: ProjectRecoveryJournal is the synchronous off-main filesystem boundary; ProjectPersistenceController will own scheduling and user-visible state

storage.pathDisclosure: the file name never contains the project name or path
storage.commit: durable flush, full readback verification, then one handle-based atomic replacement

schema.packagePath: canonical package path encoded as UTF-8 for future recovery UI
schema.projectGeneration: exact runtime generation that produced the snapshot
schema.revision: exact runtime revision that produced the snapshot
schema.persistedStateId: persisted state identity; must differ from stateId
schema.baselineProjectJsonSha256: SHA-256 of the exact live project.json bytes read before journal commit
schema.projectJsonSha256: SHA-256 of the canonical recovery project payload
schema.project: complete project source DOM including unknown fields

write.serialization: one process-wide cancellable mutation gate prevents concurrent journal replacement or retirement
write.cancellation: checked before and between snapshot, baseline read, serialization, staging, write, flush, verification, and commit
write.failure: the previous complete journal remains installed and every admitted staging file is removed

inspection.recoverable: journal baseline SHA-256 exactly equals the current live project.json SHA-256
inspection.redundant: the current live project.json also equals the recovery payload and no recovery choice is needed
inspection.staleBaseline: candidate metadata is returned but the payload must not be applied automatically
inspection.corrupt: malformed structure, identity, hash, dirty state, or payload fails explicitly

retirement.ordering: journal revision must not be newer than the committed revision
retirement.deletion: deletes the validated open file handle, never an unchecked path target

qtIntegration.executor: the existing process-lifetime serial project persistence pool
qtIntegration.supersession: Save and Save As cancel pending or admitted recovery writes before queueing package persistence
qtIntegration.saveFailure: a failed Save re-arms recovery protection for the unchanged dirty state without re-arming package autosave
qtIntegration.recoveryFailure: an unchanged failed recovery write remains terminal until a newer runtime publication
qtIntegration.saveSuccess: retire the old package identity using the committed generation and revision before reporting completion
qtIntegration.shutdown: cancel and drain admitted recovery work together with any admitted Save
